topics.title: Meaning of First Aid | Meaning of First Aid Box | Uses of First Aid Box Primary 4 (Basic 4) - Home Economics
topics.content:
HOME ECONOMICS
PREVOCATIONAL STUDIES
SECOND TERM
PRIMARY 6
WEEK 9 - MEANING, CONTENT AND USES OF FIRST BOX
PREVIOUS LESSON - Prevention of Home and School Accidents (Primary 6)
TOPIC - FIRST AID
LEARNING AREA
1. Introductory Activities
2. Meaning of First Aid
3. Meaning of First Aid Box
4. Uses of First Aid Box
5. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most of the pupils should have attained the following objectives -
1. describe first aid.
2. differentiate between first aid and first aid box.
3. list items inside first aid box.
4. state the uses of first aid box.
ENTRY BEHAVIOURS
The pupils can identify and state the uses of Items inside the first aid box.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
first aid box and its contents
school’s first aid box
charts
pictures
textbooks
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
Scheme of Work
9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
Course Book
All Relevant Material
Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Display some of the items in a first aid box for the pupils to identify and discuss.
Pupil’s Activities - This is bandage, scissor, cotton, etc.
Teacher’s remark - Correct. The above items are contents of first aid box. Discuss the meaning of first aid and first aid box and summary the key points on the board.
MEANING OF FIRST AID
Many lives are saved through first aid, given before the emergency services arrived.
First aid is the immediate care and support give to someone who is injured or slicked. First aid is given by a qualified person.
MEANING OF FIRST AID BOX
A first aid box is a collection of supplies and equipment that is used to give medical treatment.
CONTENT OF FIRST AID BOX (KIT)
A basic first aid kit may contain:
1. First aid books
2. Bondages
3. Scissors
4. Cotton wool
5. Gentia violet
6. Guaze
7. Iodine
8. Plaster of different sizes
9. Thermometer
10. Safety pins
11. Hand towel
12. Antiseptic (Dettol)
13. Cleansing agent/soap
14. Splint, etc.
ASSIGNMENT
Find out the uses of each item in a first aid box.
LESSON 2 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Based the previous assignment, ask the pupils to state the uses of first aid box.
Pupil’s Activities - First aid box is used….
Teacher’s remark - Listen to the pupils, Comment, discuss and summary some of the uses of first aid box on the board
USES OF FIRST AID BOX
A first aid box is a collection of supplies and equipment that is used to give immediate treatment. These collections served the following purpose:
1. It is used for giving immediate care and support to patients.
2. It is used for reducing infections.
3. It is used to save live.
4. It is used for reducing the time of recovery.
5. It is used for reducing pain.
6. It is used for preventing/reducing excessive blood loss.
7. It used for preventing the condition of the patients from getting from worse.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Shows the contents of a First Aid Box to pupils and lets the pupils identify each of the contents of first aid box.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify content of first aid box.
3. Discuss the meaning of first aid and first aid box.
Pupil’s Activities - Listen to the teacher’s explanation.
4. Discuss the uses of first aid box.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in the class discussion.
5. Guides and lets the pupils state the uses of each materials in first box.
Pupil’s Activities - State the uses of first aid materials.
6. Summary the key points on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
1. describe first aid.
2. differentiate between first aid and first aid box.
3. state 5 items inside first aid box.
WORKBOOK
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT (TEST)
1. Many lives are saved through ________ given before the emergency services arrived.
A. first aid
B. second aid
C. third aid
2. ________ is the immediate care and support give to someone who is injured or slicked.
A. first aid
B. second aid
C. third aid
3. First aid is given by a ________ person.
A. unqualified
B. qualified
C. any
4. First aid is the immediate care and support give to someone who is ________.
A. sicked
B. injured
C. both sicked and injured
5. ________ is a collection of supplies and equipment that is used to give medical treatment.
A. first aid
B. first aid box
C. first aids
6. First aid is the ________ care and support give to someone who is injured or slicked.
A. last
B. first
C. immediate
7. First aid is the ________ given to any person suffering a sudden illness or injury, with care provided to preserve life, prevent the condition from worsening, or to promote recovery.
A. first aids
B. first aid
C. assistance
Underline the item of first aid box.
7. Rope, Antiseptic, Cotton wool, Wool
8. Bandage, Rope, Water, Hand glove
Underline items not inside first aid box.
7. Rope, Antiseptic, Cotton wool, Wool
8. Bandage, Rope, Water, Hand glove

HOME ECONOMICS

LEARNING AREA

2. Factors Influencing Choice of Personal Belongings
3. Uses of Personal Belongings
4. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, the pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and able to -
1. state factors Influencing choice of personal belongings;
2. explain the uses of personal belongings.
ENTRY BEHAVIOR
Pupil’s school materials, clothes, shoes, toothbrush, etc.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Pictures and charts of some personal belongings
2. Some real objects
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
Scheme of Work
9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
Course book
All Relevant Materials
Online Materials
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
Personal belongings are items (things) that are belong to one person.
For example -  clothes, shoes, towel, underwear, toothbrush, wristwatch, etc.
These items are used everyday and not to be shared with anyone.
CHOICE OF PERSONAL BELONGINGS
Choice of personal belongings is an act of choosing particular items many alternatives.
The choice you made describe what belongs to you.
FACTORS INFLUENCE CHOICE OF PERSONAL BELONGINGS
There are a lot of factors that influence the choice of personal belongings. These are -
1. Money
2. Sex
3. Age
4. Weather
5. Choice - Likes and dislikes
6. Religion
7. Family
8. Style
9. Association
LESSON 2 - USES OF PERSONAL BELONGINGS
1. Toothbrush
It is used for brushing the teeth.
2. Hair brush and comb
It is used for bushing or combing the hair.
3. Soap and Sponge
It is used for washing the body.
4. Towel
It is used for cleaning the body.
5. Shoes
It is used for protecting the feet against sharp objects and other harmful things.
6. Clothes
It is used for covering, protecting and beautifying the body.
7. Bags
It is used for carrying personal items from place to place.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Guides class discussion on factors Influencing choice of personal belongings.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate in the discussion.
3. Explain the uses of personal belongings.
Pupil’s Activities - State the uses of personal belongings.
4. Summary the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Care of Personal Belongings Primary 4 (Basic 4) - Home Economics
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupil to:
1. mention 5 factors that influence choice of personal belongings:
2. explain the uses of the following:
- Toothbrush
- Hair brush
- Soap and Sponge
- Towel

WEEKLY ASSIGNMENT (TEST)

A. Personal belongings
B. Family belongings
C. Friend belongings

A. Soap and Sponge
B. Comb
C. Toothbrush
3. ________ is used for bushing or combing the hair.
A. Soap and Sponge
B. Comb
C. Toothbrush
4. ________ is used for washing the body.
A. Soap and Sponge
B. Comb
C. Toothbrush

A. Shoes
B. Towel
C. Clothes
6. ________ is used for protecting the feet against sharp objects and other harmful things.
A. Shoes
B. Towel
C. Clothes

A. Shoes
B. Towel
C. Clothes

B. Bags
C. Clothes

C. Choice of universal belongings

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
Choice of personal belongings is an act of choosing particular items many alternatives. The choice you made describe what belongs to you.
When choosing items of your choice, be sure it is right and suit your personal appearance.
RIGHT CHOICE (MEANING)
The right choice is an act of deciding what is good and best for you.
MEANING OF PERSONAL APPEARANCE
Appearance is your own personal image that you give out to other people.
The way you dress, you will be addressed. If your personal appearance is good and great, people will respect and treat you well.
Your personal appearance are you totality.
EFFECTS OF RIGHT CHOICE AND USES ON PERSONAL APPEARANCE
1. It make you look beautiful and neat.
2. You will feel cool and comfortable in them.
3. People will admired you because of the way you look.
4. People will compliment you.
5. It will give you a sense of belonging in the midst of people.
LESSON 2 - EFFECTS OF RIGHT CARE ON PERSONAL APPEARANCE
1. It saves money.
2. It is durable.
3. It saves time and money.

2. Uses of various rooms in a house
3. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most of the pupils should have attained the following objectives -
1. identify various rooms in a house.
2. identify the uses of various rooms in a house.
3. Attempt 70% (and above) assessment test correctly.
ENTRY BEHAVIOURS
The pupils can identify and state the uses of various rooms in a house or building.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Pictures of various functional rooms in a house.
2. Pictures of uses of various rooms in a house.
METHOD OF TEACHING

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
A room is a space occupied in a house. A room is one of the separate parts of the inside of a house. Different rooms have different facilities based on their uses.
There are many rooms in a house which serves different purpose.
1. Sitting room
2. Bedroom
3. Dining room
4. Kitchen
5. Food store
6. Bathroom
7. Toilet
USES OF SITTING ROOM AND BEDROOM
USES OF SITTING ROOM
1. It is used for welcoming our guests.
2. It is used for entertainment.
3. It is used for relaxation.
USES OF BEDROOM
1. It is used for resting.
2. It is used for resting.
3. It is used for dressing up.
3. It is used for keeping and safeguarding our personal belongings.
USES OF FOOD STORE
1. It is used for keeping our food items.
2. It is used to keeping pests and Insects away from our foodstuffs.
3. It is used for keeping our foodstuffs from food diseases.
4. It is used for keeping our kitchen tools and equipments.
LESSON 2 - USES OF VARIOUS FUNCTIONAL ROOMS IN A HOUSE
Continuation…..
USES OF BEDROOM
1. It is used for our bathing.
2. It is used used for urinating.
3. It is used for washing dirty parts of body.
4. It is used for brushing our tooth.
5. It is used for washing our clothes.
USES OF TOILET
1. It is used for defecating.
2. It is used for urinating.
USES OF KITCHEN
1. It is used for cooking our foods.
2. It is cleaning our kitchen utensils.
3. It is used for serving food.
USED OF DINING ROOM
1. It is used for eating our meals.
2. It is used for entertaining our guests.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Presents pictures or charts of various rooms in a house.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify the various rooms in a house with the help of a teacher.
3.Presents another picture showing various uses of the room.
Pupil’s Activities - Give examples using their own homes.
4. Summary the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.

PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most of the pupils should have attained the following objectives -
1. Identify various rooms in a house.
2. State how to keep the kitchen and dining clean daily.
3. Carry out daily cleaning of the house.
4. Attempt 70% (and above) assessment test correctly.
ENTRY BEHAVIOURS
The pupils can identify and state the tools and equipments used for cleaning various rooms in a house or building.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Pictures of various functional rooms in a house.
2. A chart of different steps involved in a daily cleaning of various functional rooms in a house.
3. Brooms, ceiling brooms, duster, dust pan, refuse bin, flower in a small vase.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
Scheme of Work
9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
Course Book
All Relevant Material

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
A room is one of the separate parts of the inside of a house. Different rooms have different facilities based on their Uses. There are many rooms in a house which serves different purpose -
1. Sitting room
2. Bedroom
3. Dining room
4. Kitchen
5. Food store
6. Bathroom
7. Toilet
KITCHEN
A kitchen room is a room in a house where meal (food) are prepared.
Kitchen and dining are side by side room.
CARE FOR THE KITCHEN
1. Daily and weekly cleaning
2. Regular sweeping
3. Removing cobwebs
4. Regular dusting and cleaning the kitchen tools and equipments.
5. Washing kitchen utensils with soap and clean water.
6. Immediately washing of pot, plate and cutlery after cooking.
LESSON 2 - DINING ROOM
A dinning room is a room in a house with dining chairs and centre table where meals are eaten.
CARE FOR THE DINING ROOM
1. Daily and weekly cleaning
2. Regular sweeping
3. Removing cobwebs
4. Regular dusting and cleaning of the chairs and table.
5. Immediately clean after eating.
6. Regular washing of the dining clothes and hand towels.
LESSON 3 - CARING FOR FUNCTIONAL ROOMS
- Reorganize the class as kitchen and dining room for the pupils to demonstrate how to care for the both.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Explains the steps involved in the daily care of kitchen and dining rooms in a house.
Pupil’s Activities - Practice in groups how to remove cobwebs, sweep, dust and arrange things in the kitchen and dining room.
3. Demonstrates daily cleaning of kitchen and dining room.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate in daily and weekly cleaning of different rooms.
4. Summarize the lesson on the board.
Copy short notes on daily cleaning of rooms.
NEXT LESSON
Care of the Bathroom and Toilet | Practical Cleaning of the Bathroom and Toilet Primary 4 (Basic 4) - Home Economics
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:

LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
MEANING OF FOOD
Foods are solid or liquid substances that gives essential nutrients to the body.
There are different kind food.
Some are in solid form while others are in liquid.
COMMON FOOD IN OUR LOCALITY
1. Solid foods
Example of solid foods are rice, bean, eba, fufu, etc.
2. Liquid foods
Liquid foods are pap, custard, tea, juice, etc.
3. Fruit foods
Fruits are in both solid and liquid forms.
REASONS FOR EATING FOOD
We eat foods for the following reasons,
1. for daily energy.
2. for protection against diseases.
3. for clear vision.
4. for growth.
5. for cleansing.
6. for social activities.
LESSON 2 - KINDS OF FOOD AND THEIR SOURCES
1. BODY BUILDING FOOD
Food that helps the body to grow and repair the worm out tissue is called protein.
Protein is a body building food.
Source of body building food includes - bean, meat, fish, eggs, cheese, milk, etc.
3. ENERGY GIVING FOOD
Energy giving foods are known as carbohydrate. It keeps the body warm and energy to the body.
Source of energy giving food includes - yam, rice, bread, garri (eba), cocoyam, etc.
4. BODY PROTECTOR FOOD
Vitamins and minerals are body protector foods. They fight against the diseases in the body.
Source of body protector food includes - fruits, vegetables, milk, eggs, liver, fish, etc.

MEANING OF FOOD
Foods are solid or liquid substances that gives essential nutrients to the body. Food nutrients are the essential substances present in the food that help the body to function well.
CLASSES OF FOOD NUTRIENTS
There are six (6) main classes of nutrients that the body needs.
These are carbohydrates, proteins, fats and oils, vitamins, minerals and water.
It is important that everyone consumes these six nutrients on a daily basis to help them build their bodies and maintain their health.
1. CARBOHYDRATES
Source of carbohydrate - rice, yam, bread, etc.
2. PROTEIN
Sources of proteins are eggs, milk, bean, etc.
3. VITAMINS
Source of vitamins - fruits like oranges, pawpaw, vegetables, etc.
4. FAT AND OILS
Source of fat and oils - palm oil, groundnut oil, vegetables oil, oily fish, butter, etc.
6. MINERALS SALT
Source of minerals salt - Iodised salt, liver, eggs, etc.
6. WATER
Source of water - drinking water, fruits juice and other drinks
LESSON 2 - FUNCTIONS OF FOOD NUTRIENTS
1. CARBOHYDRATE
Carbohydrate supplies heat and energy to play.
2. PROTEIN
Proteins builds the body and repair body tissue.
3. VITAMIN
Vitamins help to fight against diseases in the body.
4. FATS AND OILS
Fats and oils keep the warm and give energy to the body.
5. WATER
Water regulates the temperature of the body.
